interpretation: Removing Atomic produced no protection-metadata improvement in the observed native fixture. Reapplying Complete through NSURL also produced no observable improvement; neither is an evidence-supported production fix.

The phenomenon occurs in standalone Objective-C before replacement and without app backup operations. Atomic-only, overwrite-only or Kotlin-reader-only explanations cannot explain the entire observed phenomenon; this does not exclude additional application defects.

Identical Complete, None and default observations do not locate causality between shared Foundation behavior and the lower-level platform. The public kernel setter did not execute, so its following sample is not evidence of a failed kernel mutation.

Missing FileManager protection remains a strict failure. URL labels, class3 and unsupported capability reports do not prove hardware protection, a universal Simulator limitation or an acceptable replacement oracle.
